source: OWASP Secure Coding Practices Quick Reference Guide v2.0 (curated subset)

rules.name: Sanitize Untrusted Data Before OS Command Execution
rules.description: All output passed to operating system commands must be sanitized against untrusted data, preventing OS command injection - directly analogous to CWE-78 and the process_exec category this pipeline detects.

rules.name: Prefer Task-Specific APIs Over Direct OS Command Invocation
rules.description: Applications should use task-specific built-in APIs to perform operating system tasks rather than issuing commands directly to the OS (e.g. via a spawned shell), which is a common vector for supply-chain droppers.

rules.name: Never Pass Untrusted Data to Dynamic Code Execution Functions
rules.description: User- or dependency-supplied data must never be passed to dynamic execution constructs such as eval() or exec(), a primary technique used by obfuscated malicious payloads to hide their true behavior until runtime.

rules.name: Verify Integrity of Libraries and Executables via Checksums
rules.description: Checksums or cryptographic hashes should be used to verify the integrity of interpreted code, libraries, executables, and configuration files before use, complementing SLSA provenance verification.

rules.name: Vet Third-Party Code and Libraries for Malicious Functionality
rules.description: Secondary applications, third-party code, and libraries should be reviewed to confirm business necessity and validate that their functionality is safe, since introducing an unreviewed dependency is a primary supply-chain attack vector.

rules.name: Implement Cryptographically Signed Auto-Updates
rules.description: If an application performs automatic updates, it should verify cryptographic signatures on the downloaded code over an encrypted channel, preventing a compromised update server or MITM from delivering a malicious payload - directly related to CWE-494 (Download of Code Without Integrity Check).

rules.name: Never Pass Untrusted Data to Dynamic Include/Import Functions
rules.description: User- or dependency-supplied data must not be passed directly to a dynamic file-include or import function, which can be abused to load and execute arbitrary, attacker-controlled code paths.

rules.name: Never Hardcode Credentials or Connection Strings in Source
rules.description: Passwords, API keys, and connection strings must never be stored in clear text within source code or client-side artifacts; they should be encrypted and stored in a protected location on a trusted system - directly related to CWE-798 (Use of Hard-coded Credentials).
